chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who has his shroud in his house will not be written among the oblivious, and he will be recompensed every time he looks at it.

key_terms.الْغَافِلِينَ: the oblivious / the heedless (those unaware of death and the afterlife)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of keeping one's shroud at home according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this practice of keeping the kafan at home serves as a tangible tool for *dhikr al-mawt* (remembrance of death), countering the spiritual negligence (*ghaflah*) that often accompanies worldly life. Scholars highlight that the continuous visual reminder transforms the mundane act of seeing the shroud into an ongoing source of reward (*ajr*), fostering a state of readiness for the inevitable transition to the afterlife.
